notes.meaning: The speaker praises the bride from her feet upward, admiring her noble walk in fine sandals. Her graceful curves are compared to jewels crafted by a skilled artist. Traditionally, this shows the Church clothed in the beauty of Christ, walking steadily to share the gospel of peace.

The bride's waist and body are pictured as a cup of mixed wine and a golden heap of harvested wheat bordered by lilies. These images point to health, plenty, and joyful nourishment. In the life of the church, this describes the rich spiritual food provided to sustain and comfort believers.

Her breasts are described as twin fawns of a gazelle, showing youthful beauty, balance, and gentleness. Early readers saw this as a picture of the church nourishing her spiritual children. It also points to the twin graces of faith and love growing together.

Her neck stands tall and pure like an ivory tower, and her quiet, sparkling eyes look like the clear pools of Heshbon. Her nose or face is compared to a stately mountain tower looking toward enemy lands. This portrays a believer who possesses clear spiritual sight and brave, watchful faith.

Her head rises with dignity like the fruitful peak of Mount Carmel, and her dark, flowing hair shines with royal purple beauty. Her appearance is so striking that the king is held captive by her charms. Spiritually, this shows how Christ delights in the beauty of his people and chooses to dwell among them.

differ.view: Some charismatics teach that believers who show deep sacrifice and devotion can hold the Lord captive in prayer, moving him to act on their behalf.

notes.meaning: The bridegroom breaks into wonder at the delightful charms of his bride. He finds complete happiness in her company and love. In the traditional reading, Christ expresses his deep joy over the church, which he has made lovely through his grace.

The bride stands tall and upright like a flourishing palm tree, bearing sweet fruit. The palm tree remains green and strong even under harsh conditions. For believers, this represents growing straight toward heaven and staying fruitful through trials.

The husband resolves to draw close, embrace the palm tree, and enjoy its fruit. He looks forward to her refreshing love and the sweet fragrance of her breath. Spiritually, Christ visits his people to enjoy the spiritual fruit and sincere devotion he produces in their hearts.

Her speech and kisses are compared to the finest wine, going down smoothly and pleasantly. Her words are so lively that they can awaken those who are drowsy or silent. When Christians speak words of grace, their conversation honors Christ and revives sluggish souls.

The bride rests in full assurance, declaring that she belongs entirely to her beloved and that his heart longs for her. This is the peak of marital security and peace. For the Christian, it is a comforting reminder that we belong to Christ and are dearly wanted by him.

differ.view: Adam Clarke noted that the husband's longing for his wife here reverses the ancient curse of the fall, restoring harmony in marriage.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters hold that the young woman is rejecting King Solomon here to remain loyal to her true love, a simple country shepherd.

notes.meaning: The bride invites her beloved to step away from city life and walk together through fields and rural villages. She longs for uninterrupted time alone with him. Believers similarly seek quiet places away from worldly distractions to enjoy close fellowship with the Lord.

She proposes rising early to inspect the spring growth of the grapevines and flowering pomegranates. In that secluded, blooming place, she promises to give him her whole heart. The soul likewise invites Christ to examine its growth and receives fresh tokens of his love in active service.

Fragrant mandrakes fill the air, and choice fruits from both this year and the past are stored at the door. The bride has kept the best of everything solely for her husband. In the same way, a devoted believer dedicates every past experience and present gift entirely to Christ's honor.
